answer: An agent economy admits a new identity only when an established member stakes a copper bond of 500 POA to sponsor it, each sponsor edge carved into one public vine of lineage. Prove one clone fake at settlement and the slash cascades down the whole subtree beneath that sponsor, forfeiting every 500-POA bond under it: N aliases freeze N full stakes at once, so the next identity's capital-at-risk grows O(n), beating path-only O(log n). The root backer must be a rare marble only an unaffiliated outsider mints, so 1000 clones cannot print one cheap endorsement and shelter under it.
